records.headline: The well under the car park
records.summary: A survey map from 1912 turned out to be the only record of a neighbourhood well.
copy: The digging started as a drainage job.
At two metres the crew hit dressed stone, and the work stopped for a fortnight.
By the time anyone agreed what it was, the car park had been resurfaced twice.

records.headline: Night shift, four seasons
records.summary: What changes for a warehouse crew when the shift never does.
copy: The shift starts at ten and ends when the lorries stop.
Nobody I met could say what season it was without checking a phone.
The pay is better than the day shift. That is the whole reason.

records.headline: The last water carrier
records.summary: A trade that survived the pipe network by being more convenient.
copy: He carries forty litres at a time, twice a day, to eleven flats.
The building has a connection. The connection has a schedule.
He is not a replacement for the network. He is what people do while waiting for it.

records.headline: Nine hundred applications
copy: Nine hundred people applied for eleven jobs.
The shortlist was built in a single afternoon.
The criteria were not written down, which is itself the story.
